To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
intermediate filament proteins interact with the adaptor complex AP3 to control the positioning and function of late endocytic organelles.
the intermediate filament cyto- skeleton is required for the correct positioning of adaptor complexes, which in turn regulate the subcellular localization of endocytic compartments.

the adaptor complex AP3 interacts with the intermediate-filament cytoskeleton, and that this interaction is required for the correct subcellular positioning of the adaptor complex, as well as for the function of the adaptor complex in the regulation of the pH and zinc content of late endocytic compartments.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of novel mechanisms of organelle positioning and function.
the role of the cytoskeleton in endo-lysosome positioning and in regulation the adaptor complex AP3.
the role of the cytoskeleton in endo-lysosomes positioning and function.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
AP-3 and the intermediate filament cytoplasm are functionally linked and that this association is important for the proper distribution of the adaptor complex and its cargoes.
intermediate filament proteins are required for the normal distribution of the adaptor complex, AP-3, and for the maintenance of the normal content of late endocytic compartments and autophagosomes.

the cytoskeleton is a key player in the organization of the endo-lysosome network, and that the intermediate filament cytoarchitecture, in particular, is required for AP-3-dependent vesicle trafficking and autophagosome formation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the intermediate filament cytoarchitecture regulates AP-3-dependent sorting, trafficking and positioning of endosomal organelles.
intermediate filaments are involved in the regulation of AP-3-dependent endocytic/autophagy pathways.
the intermediate filament cytoarchitecture regulates the AP-3-dependent sorting machinery.
The main takeaway from our work is that
cytoskeletal networks control endo-lysosome positioning and function by interacting with the adaptor complex AP3, a key player in endocytic sorting.
intermediate filament proteins, through their interaction with AP-3, contribute to the regulation of the subcellular positioning of AP-3 and the endo-lysosome compartment.
the intermediate filament cytoarchitecture is required to position AP-3 and the late endocytic compartments in the cell.
